title: refactor(client): retire environments.updateVisibility and delete the orphaned dispatcher route table
body:
Fixes #17964

Clause-②: no

Ruling of record: comment `5653315449` on #17964 — director-seat decision batch #132 item 1, **letter A**, maintainer 「同意」 2026-09-13. Its four numbered items are this PR's whole scope; the direction was not re-opened and nothing was widened past them.

## Item 1 — `environments.updateVisibility` is removed from the published SDK

`client.environments.updateVisibility(id, visibility)` is gone from `packages/client/src/index.ts`. Its only behaviour was a write the control plane refuses: it PATCHed the generic `/api/v1/cloud/environments/:id` route with `{ visibility }`, and `visibility` is one of the server-owned columns that route rejects — the same accept-set (`display_name`, `is_default`, `metadata`) the sibling `update` docblock already records. Its own docblock described a whole capability that does not exist, and the 2026-09-12 maintainer ruling puts that capability on its **own** endpoint when public listing ships, so this method was never going to be its carrier.

- **Changeset** `.changeset/17964-environments-updatevisibility-retired.md`: `@objectstack/client: minor` with the **BREAKING** banner (the `major`-class change recorded under the launch-window convention), the `Clause-②: no` line, and the ADR-0087 disposition marker. The gate reads it as `not-required (runtime-interface-only) -- verified: packages/client/src/index.ts#ObjectStackClient (class)`.
- **ADR-0087 semantic entry as a structured TODO**, left at the removal site: a call site has no conversion — `objectstack migrate meta` rewrites stored metadata, and an SDK call site is not stored metadata — so the TODO (surface · reason · acceptance) naming the method and pointing at the future endpoint is the channel that exists. It also says, in as many words, that restoring this signature is the one thing not to do when that endpoint lands.
- **The pins prove the removal, not what remains.** The presence pin in `client.environments-namespace.test.ts` was replaced by an absence pin at both layers, each carrying a live control on the un-retired sibling `updateHostname`.

## Item 2 — the orphaned route-table docblock is deleted

`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts` loses the control-plane route table that sat between `handlePackages` and `resolveActiveOrganizationId` (located from those symbols, never from a line number). The ruling's characterisation was **verified before deleting**: after the deletion the file's only remaining `/cloud/` occurrences are the guards that SKIP those paths (`extractEnvironmentIdFromPath` returns `undefined` for `/cloud/environments/`, and `/cloud` is in `skipPaths`), plus prose. Nothing in this repo serves `/cloud/drivers` or `/cloud/environments*` at all — the routes belong to `objectstack-ai/cloud` and the only in-repo callers are the SDK's own `fetch` calls. Comment-only; no runtime byte moves.

## Item 3 — the control-plane reading is an acceptance NOTE, not a gate

⛔ Not attempted here and ⛔ not a gap: this session has no control-plane reach, and the ruling says the letter does not depend on it. It stays for a seat that has that reach to record on the card.

## Item 4 — `Clause-②: no`

A published surface **shrinks**. No export is added, no accept set widens, no schema key or closed-set member appears. `check:changeset-gate-self-tests` and the ADR-0087 gate both pass on the declaration.

## Premises falsified first — all three held, and the third was measured

1. **`Clause-②: no`.** Verified by direction: the diff removes a published member and adds none. Nothing in it can grade `yes`.
2. **The docblock is orphaned.** Verified at the symbols, as above — the file serves none of the routes it listed.
3. **`updateVisibility` has no in-repo caller — this was NOT measured before and now is.** A tree-wide sweep (`git grep` over the whole checkout: `packages`, `apps`, `examples`, tests, docs) finds **zero** call sites. The zero is a reading, not a bare grep: the control word `updateHostname` — the sibling method declared eight lines above it — lit **8** hits in the same sweep, including the parallel type pin in the very test file that had to change. After the change the only live reference anywhere is the absence pin; every other hit is prose or release-owned changelog history, which is not edited.

## Verification

- **Gate families** — `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` from the actual changed paths, every family run, reconciled with `--ran`: **61 derived / 61 run / 0 NOT-MEASURED / 0 UNRUN**.
  - One red, and it is not this PR's: `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` exits 1 naming `packages/cli/test/init-created-files-summary.e2e.test.ts` — pre-existing wherever `packages/spec/dist` is built, already filed as #18353 / #18348.
  - Two families first answered `exit 3` / a prerequisite refusal because this checkout had no full `dist` (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:skill-examples`). Neither was recorded as a pass: the tree was built and both were re-run to a real **exit 0**.
- **`pnpm lint`, repo-wide, unnarrowed** — `eslint . --no-inline-config`, exit **0**, 76s, zero findings. Measured over the whole repository, so no narrowing has to be declared.
- **`packages/client`** — `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` + `check:test-typecheck`) exit 0; `pnpm test` **43 files / 524 tests passed**.
- **`packages/runtime`** — `typecheck` exit 0; full `pnpm test` **263 files / 3647 tests passed** (the 22 `http-dispatcher*` suites, 484 tests, were also run on their own first).
- **Dependency closure built before any verdict** — `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/client^...' --filter @objectstack/client build` (35 packages), then a repo-wide turbo build so the dist-reading gates had something real to read.
- **The removal is measured at the published artefact, with two live controls.** Member declarations in the built `packages/client/dist/index.d.ts`: `updateVisibility` **0**, `updateHostname` **1**, `rotateCredential` **1**. In the shipped `dist/index.mjs`: `updateVisibility` **0**, `updateHostname` **1**.

### Reverse verification — both absence pins were driven RED, then restored

One-shot proof, run from the committed state, mutation leg and restore leg symmetric. The pin suite imports `./index` relatively, so it reads this checkout's **source**, not `dist` — no rebuild is in the loop and none is needed. Each leg proved the edit reached disk before anything was read: the mutation took the file's blob hash off its HEAD value and `updateVisibility: async` from 0 occurrences to 1; the restore put the hash back to the HEAD blob exactly, under an `EXIT INT TERM` trap with absolute paths.

| leg | runtime pin (`vitest`) | type pin (`check:test-typecheck`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| at HEAD (method absent) | exit 0 — 11 passed | exit 0 — 0 errors |
| method re-inserted | exit **1** — `AssertionError: expected true to be false` on the `in` check | exit **1** — TS2578 unused `@ts-expect-error`, named in that file |

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope for this card, noted rather than filed, and nothing here is fixed in this PR:

- `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`: the docblock now immediately above `resolveActiveOrganizationId` reads "Resolve the calling **user id** from the request session" — it describes a different method from the one it is attached to. Pure prose inaccuracy in a file this PR touches; not a defect, not a contract breach, not an authoring trap, so it is noted here rather than carded. Who would meet it: the next PR that edits this method's body.
- `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts` still carries two prose mentions of `/cloud/*` inside the skip guards. They are correct — they document why the path is skipped — and are deliberately kept: deleting them would remove the explanation for the very behaviour the deleted table made look ambiguous.

⛔ No label, assignee, ready flip, auto-merge arming or enqueue was performed — landing is the PM seat's act.
